item.title: Nagato Wagyu: Grilling Yamaguchi's Prized Beef — Guide
item.description: Yamaguchi is proud of its wagyu, and the Nagato area on the northern coast is known for beautifully marbled local beef. The most enjoyable way to eat it is yakiniku — grilling bite-sized pieces yourself over charcoal or a hot plate at your table, cooking each cut to your liking and eating it hot off the grill with dipping sauces. The rich marbling of good wagyu melts as it sears, giving an intense, buttery flavour, and doing the grilling yourself makes it interactive and fun.

item.title: Tsuruhashi: Osaka's Korea Town and Yakiniku Warren — Guide
item.description: Tsuruhashi is the heart of Osaka’s Korean community and one of the most sensory food districts in Japan. The moment you leave the station you are in a dense warren of covered lanes packed with yakiniku grills, kimchi vendors, Korean grocers and stalls of tteok and jeon, the air permanently thick with charcoal smoke. The area grew from a postwar black market around a large Zainichi Korean population, and it remains the best place in western Japan to eat grilled meat: hundreds of restaurants, from cramped smoky counters to polished specialists, packed into a few blocks.

item.title: Kumano Beef: Wakayama's Mountain-Raised Wagyu — Guide
item.description: Kumano beef (Kumano-gyu) is Wakayama’s premium wagyu brand, raised in small numbers in the mountains of the Kii Peninsula where clean air, pure water and careful feeding produce beef with fine marbling and a notably sweet fat. Because production is small compared with the famous national brands, it is mostly eaten within the region, making it something of a local secret — served as grilled steak, yakiniku, shabu-shabu or in donburi at restaurants around Tanabe, Shingu and the Kumano area.

item.title: Gunma Wagyu & Yakiniku: Premium Grilled Beef from the Mountains — Guide
item.description: Gunma produces several respected wagyu beef brands, including Jomo Wagyu, raised on the prefecture’s cool mountain pastures under careful breeding and feeding standards that produce fine, even marbling and a rich, tender flavour. The beef is served throughout Gunma in dedicated yakiniku (grilled meat) restaurants, where diners grill thin-cut slices themselves at the table, as well as in steakhouses and traditional sukiyaki and shabu-shabu preparations, offering visitors an accessible taste of high-grade Japanese beef outside the more famous Kobe and Matsusaka brands.
